guide_line: Say where each particle sits, and what the gold foil showed about the atom.
steps: Thomson's cathode-ray tube found a negative particle, the electron. It stays outside the nucleus and has far less mass than a proton or a neutron.
Rutherford shot positive alpha particles at gold foil. Most went straight through, so the atom is mostly empty space. A few bounced back off a tiny, heavy, positive nucleus.
Protons and neutrons sit in that nucleus. A proton has charge 1+. A neutron has no charge. Their masses are nearly the same, and each is about 1 amu.
One element can have atoms of different mass. Those atoms are isotopes. They share a proton count and differ in neutrons.

worked_example.q: In the gold-foil experiment, a few alpha particles bounced backward. What part of the atom did they hit?
steps: Most alpha particles passed through, so the atom is not a solid packed ball.
The few that reversed hit a tiny, heavy, positive center. That center is the nucleus.

similar_problem.q: Thomson's cathode-ray tube produced a beam that moved toward a positive plate. What particle is that beam?
similar_problem.hint: The beam is negative and comes from inside the atom. Name the particle, not the scientist.

problems.q: Who used a cathode-ray tube to show that atoms contain electrons?
problems.why: Thomson's cathode-ray beam was a stream of electrons, so atoms contain negative particles.
hints: A cathode-ray tube sent a negative beam out of the atom. Name the scientist tied to that tube.

problems.q: Where are electrons found, compared with the nucleus?
problems.why: Electrons are outside the nucleus. They are not packed into the positive center.
hints: Electrons make the negative region around the atom. They are not inside the positive center. Say where they stay.

problems.q: Who showed that the atom has a small, dense, positive nucleus?
problems.why: Rutherford's gold-foil experiment sent most alpha particles straight through and bounced a few back. The bounce requires a small positive nucleus.
hints: A few alpha particles bounced off thin gold foil. Name the scientist who ran that experiment.

problems.q: Who showed that the nucleus contains a neutral particle, the neutron?
problems.why: Chadwick identified the neutron: a nuclear particle with no charge and about the same mass as a proton.
hints: The nucleus needed a heavy particle with zero charge. Name the scientist who identified it.

problems.q: Which of the proton, neutron, and electron has the smallest mass?
problems.why: A proton and a neutron each have a mass near 1 amu. An electron is far lighter.
hints: The proton and the neutron are each about 1 amu. Pick the particle that is far lighter.

problems.q: What are atoms called when they are the same element but have different masses?
problems.why: Isotopes share an atomic number and differ in mass because they differ in neutrons.
hints: Same proton count, different mass. Give the name for that pair of atoms.

problems.q: What particle makes up a cathode-ray beam?
problems.why: A cathode ray is a stream of electrons, the negative particles from inside the atom.
hints: Cathode rays are the negative pieces found inside every atom. Name the particle.

problems.q: A cathode-ray beam moves toward a positive plate. What is the sign of the particle's charge?
problems.why: Opposite charges attract. A beam pulled toward a positive plate is negative.
hints: The cathode-ray beam moves toward a positive plate. Give the sign of its charge.

problems.q: Positive alpha particles are pushed away by the center of the atom. What is the sign of the nucleus?
problems.why: Like charges repel. Positive alpha particles bounce off a positive nucleus.
hints: Positive alpha particles are repelled by the center of the atom. Give the sign of that center.

problems.q: In the gold-foil experiment, most alpha particles went straight through. What is most of the atom's volume?
problems.why: If the atom were solid packed matter, the particles would all deflect. Straight paths mean the volume is mostly empty space.
hints: Nearly every alpha particle passed straight through the foil. Say what most of the atom's volume must be.

problems.q: What did the rare alpha particle that reversed direction strike?
problems.why: Only a tiny, heavy, positive center can turn a fast alpha particle around. That center is the nucleus.
hints: The rare alpha particle that reversed direction struck the tiny heavy center. Name that center.

problems.q: What is the positive particle in the nucleus with a charge of 1+?
problems.why: A proton sits in the nucleus, has charge 1+, and is much heavier than an electron.
hints: The positive particle inside the nucleus has a charge of 1+. Name that particle.
